Verify SQL Lab blocks disallowed functions (e.g. version()). Superset enforces the block via its structured error framework and returns HTTP 500 with errors[].message 'SQL statement contains disallowed function(s): {...}' (SupersetErrorsException, issue 1030) — a deliberate security REJECTION, not a crash. The test therefore requires a rejection status (400/422/500, NOT 200 which would mean the query executed) AND that the error message names the disallowed-function block.

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the interactive SQL editor surface. Check for: (1) a code editor area with SQL syntax highlighting; (2) a database / schema selector control; (3) a results table area; (4) a saved-query or query-history section; (5) clearly visible run / stop controls. Score: 5=all present with good layout, 4=most present, 3=basic editor exists, 2=minimal SQL surface, 1=page renders but no editor, 0=missing or broken.

nodes.description: Chart visualization system quality: the charting library integration, multiple chart types, explore page design

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the chart visualisation system. Check for: (1) a charting library integration with a clear configuration story; (2) support for multiple chart types (bar / line / pie / table / big-number / ...); (3) a chart-type plugin or registry pattern that allows extension; (4) a data-transformation pipeline from query results to chart props; (5) a typed chart configuration schema; (6) responsive rendering. Score: 6=10+ chart types with plugin pattern, 5=5+ chart types and solid abstractions, 4=working charts with basic types, 3=some visualisation capability, 2=minimal rendering, 1=code exists but broken, 0=no visualisation system.

nodes.description: Dashboard builder UX quality: layout system, chart embedding, JSON metadata structure

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the dashboard listing / builder UI. Check for: (1) a list view with title / owner / status columns; (2) create and edit actions; (3) navigation into individual dashboards; (4) published / draft state indicators; (5) bulk action support. Score: 5=full-featured, 4=good listing, 3=basic list, 2=minimal page, 1=empty page, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Dashboard native filter and cross-filter design quality: filter state management, KeyValue store integration

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the dashboard filter system architecture. Check for: (1) a filter configuration persisted within the dashboard metadata; (2) filter-state persistence using a key-value or session store API; (3) cross-filter support letting one chart filter another; (4) filter scope configuration (which charts are affected); (5) default filter values handling. Score: 5=comprehensive cross-filtering, 4=native filters with state persistence, 3=basic filter support, 2=minimal, 1=incomplete, 0=missing.

nodes.description: API error handling quality: structured error responses, meaningful messages, proper HTTP status codes

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the API error handling quality based on the captured responses. Check for: (1) structured JSON error envelopes (no HTML error pages); (2) meaningful error messages explaining what went wrong; (3) correct HTTP status codes (400 for validation, 404 for not-found, 422 for unprocessable); (4) consistent format across endpoints (a `message` field); (5) no stack traces or internal details leaked to clients in production. Score: 5=excellent structured errors, 4=good structure, 3=JSON but generic, 2=mixed JSON and HTML, 1=mostly HTML, 0=crashes on error.

nodes.description: OpenAPI specification completeness and accuracy: endpoint coverage, schema definitions, response examples

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the OpenAPI / API documentation quality. Check for: (1) comprehensive endpoint coverage (dashboards, charts, datasets, data sources, queries, reports, RLS, tags, security APIs); (2) proper request / response schemas with field types; (3) authentication requirements documented; (4) query parameter documentation for filtering and pagination; (5) HTTP method and status code documentation. Score: 5=20+ endpoints with schemas, 4=most documented, 3=major endpoints, 2=partial, 1=minimal, 0=none.

nodes.description: the ORM data model quality: relationship definitions, mixins, proper indexing, migration structure

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the data model design (any ORM / language). Check for: (1) model class / record definitions whose typed columns match the spec (integer, string, text, boolean, datetime, JSON); (2) foreign key relationships with bidirectional navigation; (3) audit fields for created_at / updated_at / created_by / updated_by; (4) many-to-many relationships using explicit association tables (dashboard-chart, datasource-user, tag-tagged-object equivalents); (5) database indexes on frequently queried columns; (6) versioned schema migrations. Score: 5=production quality with full relationships and audit mixins, 4=good design with most relationships, 3=basic models, 2=minimal relationships, 1=files exist but incomplete, 0=no models.

nodes.description: RBAC permission system architecture: role hierarchy, permission view menus, data access patterns

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the RBAC permission system architecture. Check for: (1) role hierarchy (admin > editor > viewer > sql-editor > public or equivalent); (2) permission-on-resource pattern (read/write on Chart, Dashboard, etc.); (3) data-level access control (database / schema / datasource); (4) a security manager / policy module separated from request handlers; (5) owner-based access control (resource owners can edit their resources); (6) a permission synchronisation mechanism on bootstrap. Score: 5=full RBAC with data-level access, 4=good role system, 3=basic role checks, 2=simple checks, 1=auth without RBAC, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Row-level security implementation quality: WHERE clause injection, role-based filter application, SQL Lab integration

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the row-level security implementation. Check for: (1) an RLS policy model with SQL clause / filter type / role / table associations; (2) WHERE clause injection at the query compilation level; (3) support for both additive per-role filters and base filters applied to all queries; (4) RLS enforcement in chart data queries; (5) optional enforcement in the SQL editor (feature flag). Score: 5=full RLS with both filter kinds and SQL editor support, 4=working clause injection, 3=basic per-role filtering, 2=model exists but no injection, 1=broken RLS code, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Report/alert scheduling system design: the task queue beat integration, notification channels, execution logging

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the report and alert scheduling design. Check for: (1) a schedule model with cron expression, chart / dashboard association, and recipient configuration; (2) alert conditions with threshold-based triggering (not-null, >, <, ...); (3) multiple notification channels (email and chat); (4) a background task that executes scheduled reports and captures screenshots; (5) execution log model tracking success / failure / error states with timestamps; (6) grace-period and retry logic. Score: 5=production quality with alerts + reports + logging, 4=working scheduler, 3=basic scheduling, 2=models without execution, 1=incomplete, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Import/export system architecture: ZIP bundle format, resource serialization, dependency resolution

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the import / export system. Check for: (1) ZIP-based export packages organised by resource type (databases / charts / dashboards / datasets / ...); (2) a metadata file capturing version, type, and timestamp; (3) dependency resolution during import (importing a dashboard pulls its charts / datasets); (4) overwrite-vs-skip conflict resolution; (5) password masking on exported connection strings. Score: 5=full with dependency resolution, 4=working ZIP IO, 3=basic serialization, 2=partial, 1=incomplete, 0=missing.

nodes.description: the task queue async task architecture: query execution pipeline, result backend, task routing

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the asynchronous task architecture. Check for: (1) a task queue configured with a message broker and result backend; (2) async query execution with proper timeout handling; (3) result storage and retrieval (cache-key based); (4) task lifecycle tracking (pending / running / success / failed / timed_out); (5) scheduled-task configuration (periodic reports, cache warming); (6) error handling and retry. Score: 5=production quality with lifecycle management, 4=working async with caching, 3=basic task queue setup, 2=configured but minimal, 1=non-functional, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Caching strategy quality: Redis integration, cache key design, warm-up mechanism, invalidation patterns

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the caching strategy. Check for: (1) a cache backend (typically Redis) with proper serialization; (2) multi-tier caching (query results, filter state, thumbnails); (3) cache key generation based on query parameters and user context; (4) a cache warm-up endpoint for dashboards; (5) cache invalidation on data / metadata changes; (6) configurable TTL per cache type. Score: 5=sophisticated multi-tier with warm-up and invalidation, 4=working cache with key management, 3=basic Redis caching, 2=simple impl, 1=config without use, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Security implementation patterns: CSRF protection, JWT guest tokens, password hashing, SQL injection prevention

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the security implementation patterns. Check for: (1) CSRF token generation and validation on state-modifying endpoints; (2) JWT (or equivalent) guest-token implementation with signing, expiry, and scope restriction; (3) secure password hashing (scrypt / bcrypt / argon2); (4) SQL injection prevention via parameterised queries and AST validation; (5) CORS configuration; (6) rate limiting on authentication endpoints. Score: 5=comprehensive security, 4=good coverage, 3=basic CSRF and auth, 2=some measures, 1=minimal, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Database discovery and introspection quality: schema/table/column browsing, metadata extraction, SQL validation

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the database discovery and introspection system. Check for: (1) connection management for multiple analytical databases; (2) a schema browser listing catalogs / schemas / tables / columns; (3) table metadata extraction (column types, primary keys, foreign keys); (4) a SQL validation endpoint; (5) a test-connection endpoint; (6) `SELECT *` generation for quick table preview. Score: 5=comprehensive multi-engine discovery, 4=good schema browser, 3=basic listing, 2=connection only, 1=models without introspection, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Dataset management quality: column/metric definitions, data type inference, virtual dataset support

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the dataset management system. Check for: (1) a dataset model linking physical tables to the analytics layer; (2) column definitions with type inference, groupability, and filterability flags; (3) metric definitions with SQL expression support (COUNT, SUM, AVG, custom expressions); (4) virtual datasets backed by SQL queries (not physical tables); (5) a column-refresh mechanism that syncs schema changes; (6) dataset duplication. Score: 5=full management with virtual datasets and metrics, 4=good column / metric definitions, 3=basic dataset-to-table mapping, 2=minimal, 1=incomplete, 0=missing.

nodes.description: Frontend accessibility: semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, color contrast

inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate the frontend accessibility compliance. Check for: (1) semantic HTML elements (nav, main, header, section, article); (2) ARIA attributes on interactive elements (role, aria-label, aria-describedby); (3) form labels associated with inputs; (4) alt text on images; (5) logical heading hierarchy (h1 > h2 > h3). Score: 5=excellent accessibility, 4=good semantic structure, 3=basic semantic elements, 2=minimal, 1=some semantic HTML without ARIA, 0=none.
